Run the same mesh and geometry with ambient/nominal/long inputs and compare time series and GTI-weighted proton flux. Large differences would establish sensitivity, not identify the correct case. +halfwidth, radial speed and density/temperature factors.
+
+At the inner boundary the selected cone blends the ambient speed toward its
+catalogue leading-edge speed, multiplies proton density and temperature by
+their prescribed enhancements, and retains Br and the optional inductive E.
+Parker tangential B is then recomputed using the changed speed. Thus changing
+speed does not change the imposed rotational ideal electric field. No magnetic
+flux rope is invented. The density is enhanced after the ambient n~v^-2 map
+has been sampled; it is not reduced again by that ambient calibration law.

+over the first/last 10% of its duration. Where cones overlap, the largest
+space-time weight wins, with later input rows winning equal weights. This

+near-Sun interaction. The 12/24-hour durations are deliberately broad scenarios,
+not observed radial thicknesses. Density4/temperature1 match the downloaded
+reviewer run's cloud convention, but remain assumptions for these events.

+peak physical values, smooth edges, overlap semantics and Parker-E coupling.
